Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend periods in Canada for 2023 (dates shown as the full span of days that give you at least one extra day off):

| Long‑Weekend | Dates (2023) | Holiday(s) |
|--------------|--------------|------------|
| New Year’s | **Dec 31 – Jan 3** | New Year’s Day (observed Jan 2) |
| Family Day (BC, ON, AB, MB, SK) | **Feb 18 – Feb 20** | Family Day (Feb 20) |
| Good Friday | **Apr 7 – Apr 9** | Good Friday (Apr 7) |
| Victoria Day | **May 20 – May 22** | Victoria Day (May 22) |
| Canada Day (observed) | **Jul 1 – Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed Jul 3) |
| Labour Day | **Sep 2 – Sep 4** | Labour Day (Sep 4) |
| Thanksgiving | **Oct 7 – Oct 9** | Thanksgiving (Oct 9) |
| Remembrance Day (observed) | **Nov 10 – Nov 12** | Remembrance Day (observed Nov 10) |

These are the federally recognized holidays that create at least a three‑day stretch (including the weekend). Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, Heritage Day in Saskatchewan, etc.) that could also give you extra days off, but the table above covers the nationwide long weekends for 2023.
